logical_review: PointFiniteBasis selects a compatible metric separately on every open subtype. Mathlib metrizableSpaceMetric preserves the inherited subtype topology, so images of local metric balls are ambient-open.

The sigma cover index is arbitrary and may have a universe independent of the ambient space. precise_refinement acts on the cover of all local balls, and on_range gives locally finite set-valued layers without requiring a countable patch family.

At x, only the cover indices of patches containing x form a finite set. A common reciprocal radius is bounded by the radius chosen in every such patch. Any refining member containing x belongs to one of those patches, so the triangle inequality shows it lies inside the prescribed neighborhood. Finiteness is local; no global Fintype or Countable hypothesis occurs.
Smirnov first refines an arbitrary metrizable open cover locally finitely, inherits metrizability through subtype inclusion embeddings, and applies the reusable point-finite basis theorem.

The final sufficiency direction adds exactly explicit T2Space and ordinary Mathlib ParacompactSpace. Existing Mathlib paracompact-Hausdorff normality supplies regularity/T3 before the registered Nagata-Smirnov theorem is used.

LocallyMetrizable says every point has an ambient-open neighborhood with metrizable inherited topology. It includes membership of the point, and adds neither local separability nor local second countability.

The forward equivalence chooses a compatible global metric to reuse Mathlib metric paracompactness. The metric and actual-metric equivalence preserve the original topology; compatibleMetric_topology proves this with reducible metric extraction, and compatible_metric_iff replaces the supplied equal topology explicitly.
public_interface: Both files have module headers, public imports and public sections. Smirnov exposes LocallyMetrizable and compatibleMetric definitions; compatibleMetric is instance-reducible.
No sorry, admit, custom axiom, unsafe declaration, implemented_by declaration or kernel/trust override appears in either proof module.
Empty spaces, empty local patches and arbitrary cardinality are allowed. Universes were verified by compilation with explicit independent u and v.
